name: Observation of Reactor Electron Antineutrino Disappearance in the RENO Experiment
title: Observation of Reactor Electron Antineutrino Disappearance in the RENO Experiment

claim.quote: Observation of Reactor Electron Antineutrino Disappearance in the RENO Experiment

summary.plain: RENO's two Korean detectors, near and far from a cluster of six reactors, clearly caught antineutrinos disappearing as they travelled, pinning down the theta_13 mixing angle.
summary.technical: In a 229-day exposure (11 Aug 2011 - 26 Mar 2012), RENO observed a far-detector-to-expectation ratio of 0.920±0.009(stat)±0.014(syst), giving sin²(2θ₁₃) = 0.113±0.013(stat)±0.019(syst) from a rate-only analysis, at 4.9σ significance.

why_it_matters.value: One of the three reactor experiments (with Daya Bay and Double Chooz) to establish a relatively large, non-zero theta_13 in 2012.
why_it_matters.quote: consistent with neutrino oscillations, with a significance of 4.9 standard deviations

significance.quote: with a significance of 4.9 standard deviations
